summary: Giei Honda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1910 to 1914. He lectured at Kyoto University, served as assistant professor there (1935–1948), and held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Kyoto University, studying under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki. He taught at Kyoto University, serving as professor (1968–1972), and later at Kyoto Sangyo University.

Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Stanford University, studying under teachers including Jan Nattier, Carl Bielefeldt, and Bernard Faure. He taught at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies and was affiliated with the Insight Meditation Center.

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Madeleine Biardeau. By 2004, he was a senior fellow at CNRS, a member of the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, and an exchange program director at FMSH.
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, supervised by Jing Yin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Giovanni Gentile was an Italian philosopher who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the University of Pisa. He held professorships at the universities of Palermo, Pisa, and Rome, and was president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giovanni Vacca was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who earned his doctorate at the University of Genoa and studied at the University of Florence. He lectured at Florence and held the chair for History and Geography of East Asia at Sapienza University.

Giovanni Verardi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Banaras Hindu, Gorakhpur, and Allahabad universities. He held academic posts at Ca' Foscari University of Venice, the University of Bologna, and as professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale."

Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency University, Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and as president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she held research fellow positions at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisho Nakano was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate from Kyushu University. He was a professor and president at Koyasan University and served as a professor at Peking University.
Giti Dutt is a PhD student at the Australian National University, studying under the supervision of Assa Doron.
Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies in 2010.

Giuseppe Bardelli was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. From circa 1849 to 1865, he served as lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa.

Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna. He served as professor of Oriental languages and Ancient Greek at Bologna and later became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.

Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca. He taught at Visva-Bharati and Dhaka, served as professor at Sapienza, and became president of IsMEO.

Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Bai Su, and Shichang Ma, and later held a post at Peking University.

Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from the University of Tokyo, studying under Taiken Kimura, Sylvain Lévi, and Junjirō Takakusu, among others. He was an assistant at the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Toyo University in 1927.

Glenn H. Mullin is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Geshe Rabten. He founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
